standard_prerequisites.name: The glueing situation for semi-local rings
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the ambient hypotheses on A, B, K and R that the two case analyses use.

core_obligations: Case (a): from the hypothesis that A^* is not contained in R, pick a unit u of A whose image in K lies in the maximal ideal of B, observe that u is a nonzerodivisor of R and that for every a in A some u^n a lies in R, and conclude A = R_u (proof lines 7375-7378).

Case (a), continued: for a nonzero x in the Jacobson radical of A use dimension one to get K = A_x, adjust x by powers of u so that it maps to a unit of B, deduce B = R_x, and conclude Spec(R) = D(x) union D(u) with D(u) = Spec(A), D(x) = Spec(B) (proof lines 7381-7392).

Case (b): if A^* is contained in R, show every element of the maximal ideal m_A lies in R, and deduce that A is integral over R by writing A/m_A as a product of fields and producing integrality equations for elements with prescribed vanishing coordinates (proof lines 7395-7406).

Case (b), continued: use that B is integrally closed to get R contained in A contained in B, use K = union of x^{-n}R for nonzero x in m_A to see that x^{-1} is not in B, so m_A is contained in m_B, and conclude that A cap m_B is a maximal ideal of A dominated by B while A tensor B -> K is not surjective (proof lines 7407-7413).
proof_roadmap: Split into the two alternatives according to whether A^* is contained in R.
In the first case realize A and B as localizations of R at suitable elements and exhibit the cover of Spec(R).
In the second case place m_A inside R, prove integrality of A over R, and compare the maximal ideals.
difficulty_reason: The lemma determines the two possible configurations for a Noetherian semi-local domain A of dimension one with a discrete valuation ring B and a common field K as in the glueing situation: either the spectra of A and B are open subschemes covering Spec(R) with K = A tensor_R B, or B dominates one of the local rings of A at a maximal ideal and A tensor B -> K is not surjective. The proof of case (a) uses a unit u of A mapping into the maximal ideal of B, shows A = R_u and then B = R_x for a suitable x, and produces the open cover Spec(R) = D(x) union D(u) (proof lines 7375-7392). Case (b) shows the maximal ideal of A lies in R, then proves A is integral over R by a determinant-style computation in the product of residue fields, and finally that m_A is contained in m_B, so that A cap m_B is a maximal ideal of A dominated by B (proof lines 7395-7413). H2: the two case analyses each require a genuine computation of localizations, and the integrality argument in case (b) is not routine bookkeeping.
